**Rewriting one deep commit message without git rebase -i**

**What**: Corrected a false claim in commit 28f347b, five commits deep on an unpushed branch, with `-i` unavailable. Sequence: `git checkout --detach <target>` → `git commit --amend -F -` → `git rebase --onto <newsha> <oldsha> <branch>`. Clean, no conflicts, no interactive editor, no GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR trick needed.

**Why**: `git rebase -i` is blocked in this environment; `--onto` does the same job for a single deep amend.

**Where**: /home/gandalf/IA/brain-issue-701-r2, branch fix/issue-701-cold-review-round-2

**Learned**: Verify the rewrite with THREE checks, not one. (1) `git diff <old-head> <new-head>` empty — the tree survived. (2) Per-commit `git diff <old> <rewritten>` empty for each counterpart — no commit's content shifted. (3) `diff <(git log --format="%s%n%b%n---" old-range) <(...new-range)` — proves ONLY the intended message changed and the order held. Also note: the brief asked for `git diff cd1fdb0 HEAD` to be empty, but that only holds if the rewrite is the ONLY change; when the round also adds real commits, the right identity check is against the pre-rewrite head, not the original base head. Tier 3 forbids amending PUBLISHED commits — this branch had no push and no PR, so it was in bounds.
